LESSON: CAPACITY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three
Subject: MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES
Strand: Measurement
Topic 2.3: Capacity
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Capacity, part of Measurement in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade three MATHEMATICAL ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: How can the capacity of a container be measured?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. measure capacity in litres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capacity in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. add capacity in litres,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Capacity in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. measure capacity in litres,

   Capacity helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. add capacity in litres,

   Capacity helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Learners are guided in purposive pairs/ groups to collect safe materials in their immediate environment for use in measuring capacity

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Learners are guided in purposive pairs/ groups to collect safe materials in their immediate environment for use in measuring capacity

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Capacity together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Self-efficacy: learner estimates the capacity of containers up to 5 litres, measure the actual capacities of the containers

and compare the measurements.

● Communication and collaboration: learners discuss and measure capacity of different containers using 1 litre

containers.

Values:
● Unity: learners in turns practice addition of capacity in litres in real life situations.

● Responsibility: learners care of the items for measuring capacity.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: learners play digital games involving capacity in real life situations with peers.

Link to other learning areas:

The learner is able to relate collection of safe materials in their immediate environment for learning to waste management in

Environmental Activities.
